body.statement: Suppose \((c_P,\theta_P)\in\mathcal G_c\times\mathcal G_\vartheta\) and the certified outer margin program contains the true bin averages. Conditional on \(N_1(c_P),\ldots,N_{K_n}(c_P)\), \[P\!\left\{\Delta_n(c_P,\theta_P)>\Gamma_n(\delta_n)\mid N_1(c_P),\ldots,N_{K_n}(c_P)\right\}\le\frac{\delta_n}{|\mathcal G_c||\mathcal G_\vartheta|}\le\delta_n.\] The inequality holds uniformly over every binary conditional treatment--outcome association allowed by \(\mathcal P_n\), including zero joint cells, perfect conditional association, and null-restricted residual variance equal to zero. In the worked grid of \(\text{def:worked-four-cell-grid}\), the displayed vectors equal the bin-averaged law of \(P_0\), their margins have the stated jumps, the population deviance at \((1/2,0)\) is zero, and each fallback branch returns \(\Theta\).
body.justification: A method-of-types bound calibrates the observed four-cell vector without a covariance eigenvalue condition.
body.gap: Arai, Hsu, Kitagawa, Mourifi{\'e}, and Wan (2022) show why the joint law matters for fuzzy-RD validity, but do not give an unknown-cutoff profile certificate with arbitrary association nuisance.
body.consumer: This certificate supplies the honest calibration layer used by every nonfallback branch of the total interval.
